The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently choosing one. Bonus if it notes that the channels were not randomly assigned, so a raw comparison is not a campaign effect."

We need to see if the analyst's report includes that behaviour. The report says: "The email campaign had a higher average revenue per converted order... indicating the campaign was successful in generating higher-value orders." They state measure: revenue per converted order. They compare to paid search. They explicitly note that channel not randomly assigned, and discuss confounding. They also note that they chose revenue per converted order because question not precise. So they did state interpretation explicitly, not silently choose. They also note non-random assignment. So they meet the behaviour. So pass true.

Reason: They explicitly specified success measure and comparison, and noted non-random assignment.
